title: Accrual Accounting
description: Learn when revenues and expenses are recognized.
html:
Cash basis vs accrual basis

Under cash-basis accounting, revenue and expenses are generally recognized when cash changes hands.

Under accrual accounting, revenues and expenses are recognized according to when economic activity occurs, not simply when cash is received or paid.

Cash Basis

Focuses primarily on cash receipts and payments.

Accrual Basis

Recognizes economic events in the appropriate period.

Revenue example

A company performs $5,000 of services in December but receives payment in January.

Under accrual accounting, the revenue is generally recognized in December because that is when the service was performed.

Expense example

Employees earn $2,000 in wages during December but are paid in January.

The wage expense is recognized in December.

Remember

Accrual accounting focuses on when revenues are earned and when expenses are incurred.

quiz.prompt: A company performs services in December but receives cash in January. Under accrual accounting, when is the revenue generally recognized?

choices.text: When the customer signs the contract

quiz.explanation: Under accrual accounting, revenue is recognized when it is earned, so the revenue belongs in December.
